nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a partner array, giving each right vertex at most one left vertex as its partner, let $k$ be a natural number and $j$ a right vertex. nodes.title: Alternating path

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a partner array on a bipartite graph with $a$ left vertices. If the augmentation step on $\mu$ fails, then no unmatched right vertex is reached within $a + 1$ rounds of the alternating search from the unmatched left vertices.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a partner array that describes a matching. If the augmentation step on $\mu$ returns a partner array $\mu'$, then $\mu'$ also describes a matching, and $\mu'$ has exactly one more matched right vertex than $\mu$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a partner array on a bipartite graph with $a$ left vertices and $b$ right vertices. nodes.title: One augmentation step

nodes.summary: If no unmatched right vertex is reached by round `k + 1`, every matching has at most as many edges as the current one plus the right vertices first reached in round `k + 1`: the unreached left vertices and the right vertices reached by round `k + 1` cover every edge.
nodes.title: One round of the layered search bounds the deficit

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a valid partner array, $M$ a matching of the bipartite graph and $f \in \mathbb{N}$. nodes.summary: In a bipartite graph with $b$ right vertices, start from the empty matching and repeat the augmentation step until it fails, at most $b + 1$ times. No matching of the graph has more edges than the resulting matching.
nodes.title: Optimality of the augmenting-path matching algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a partner array on a bipartite graph with $a$ left vertices that describes a matching. nodes.summary: For a partner array $\mu$ of a bipartite graph with $a$ left vertices and a natural number $d$, the first free round of $\mu$ equals $d$ if and only if $d \le a$, some unmatched right vertex is reached within $d + 1$ rounds of the layered search, and for every $k < d$ no unmatched right vertex is reached within $k + 1$ rounds.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a valid partner array and $c$ a natural number such that the first free round of $\mu$, if defined, is at least $c$. nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a valid partner array (a matching of the graph) whose first free round is defined, equal to some $d$. If a left vertex $i$ is unmatched in the flip of $\mu$ along the concatenation of all the paths of the phase of $\mu$, then $i$ is unmatched in $\mu$.

nodes.summary: Given a partner array $\mu$, which assigns to each right vertex $j$ either a left vertex $\mu(j)$ as partner or no partner, a left vertex $i$ is unmatched (free) when no right vertex $j$ has $\mu(j) = i$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a valid partner assignment of a bipartite graph (a matching) whose first free round is $d$. Then every path of the phase of $\mu$ has exactly $d + 1$ pairs.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
